content.thinking: The page is headed with how to invest cheaply in an index over time, and the TA-125 option is already selected; my son wrote this task, and I'll leave the sum and monthly deposit as they are.

Picked out the figures so far: 70,000 ₪ put in over 120 months, and the cheaper option leaves 86,045 ₪ after 10 years. I'm skipping the terms I don't recognise (זוג, דמי משמרת, מחקה) and will look at the fund details next.
Hapoalim's account costs 6,530 and Psagot's 1,049, and the top fund by value is Psagot at 86,045. I'm going to check one or two more screens to find out which fund this is.

Several foreign companies and a fund's details, including a 0.1% management fee and some negative yearly returns, have been reviewed, and the user has stopped feeling anxious after seven screens. I'll pause here until they're ready to continue.

input.answer: If I go by the page, I'd hold the account at Psagot (marked "הזול"), buy "אי.בי.אי. מחקה ת"א 125 (4A)" (number 5112628), and end up with about 86,045 ₪ after 10 years on 70,000 ₪ put in. But I wouldn't do it alone: it isn't my bank, I'm not sure what the "‎−0.04%" next to the fund means, and I'll ask my son before I sign anything.

stuck.why: I didn't understand what 'הזוג' / 'הזוג הבא בתור' means. A pair of what? I guessed it means the account and the fund together.
'‎−0.04%' and 'בשנה · שנה אחת' look to me like the fund lost money last year. It frightened me, and I don't know if that's what it means.
'להשקיע במדד': to me מדד is the price index on the news. Only the words 'מאה עשרים וחמש החברות' told me this was the right thing.
My bank is lower down, and I didn't know if the small number under the big one (1,049 / 6,530) is what they take or something else.
